digest.component_or_area: bridge status / reconciler canary / durable state
propositions: Replace duplicate pass-record producers with a single process-finalizer writer that records minimal authoritative JSON to refs/reconciler/last-pass before releasing refs/reconciler/lock, using observed-OID CAS with bounded retry (three attempts, 100/200 ms backoff) and loud failure on push/network/permission errors.

Canonical 'rebar bridge status' and hidden compatibility alias 'rebar bridge-status' must share identical parser, options, output, errors, and exits, with status implemented as fast read-only snapshot that never mutates, calls steal(), or waits for lease.

Status verdict precedence is PAUSED > RUNNING > FOREIGN > FAILED > STALE > HEALTHY with NEVER_RUN only when no record and no live lock; canary detects CRASHED by comparing two read-only live-fence snapshots across the lock-carried lease.

Local and CI identities are segregated: explicit REBAR_ENV_ID wins; otherwise writer/status derive stable local:<repo-env-id> from checkout .env-id, which is a hard configuration error if missing/empty/unreadable; LEGACY_JIRA_ENV_ID and inbound event metadata remain unchanged.

Canary transitions from GitHub Actions heartbeat polling to durable git state by defaulting to status source after one durable producer write, with explicit REBAR_CANARY_HEARTBEAT_SOURCE=github-api retained for one-release rollback, making no heartbeat API query on the canonical path.

Rich detail is one rolling .bridge_state/last-pass.json file that safely degrades when absent or mismatched; status includes detail only when pass and environment ids match the authoritative ref; canary waits observed lease_secs (default 120, fail if over 480) and rejects after two snapshots showing unchanged OID/fence.
